examples.solution_text:
(a) Medians: $A=46$, $B=52$. Class B has the higher median because $52>46$.
(b) Class A: range $=88-13=75$, IQR $=63-29=34$.
Class B: range $=81-19=62$, IQR $=59-38=21$.
Class B has the smaller IQR, so its middle half is more consistent. It also has the smaller range.
(c) Class A has the higher maximum, $88>81$. The maximum is the best single mark; the median describes the middle of the marks. They need not give the same comparison.

(a) Both medians are $44$ and both maximums are $91$.
(b) Class C: range $=91-11=80$. Class D: range $=91-4=87$. Class D has the larger range.
(c) Class C: IQR $=61-26=35$. Class D: IQR $=54-33=21$.
Class D has the smaller IQR, so its middle half is more consistent, even though its full range is larger.

(a) Crew A has the lower median: $31<36$ minutes, so it generally finishes faster.
(b) $33$ minutes is below Crew B’s median of $36$ minutes. Using the box plot, estimate less than half the times were below $33$ minutes.
(c) $36$ minutes is the median, so the estimate is about $50\%$. Repeated times can affect the exact numbers above or below a threshold.

(a) Team R's median is $26$ and Team S's median is $69$. Team S has the higher median because $69>26$.
(b) Team R: IQR $=35-18=17$.
Team S: IQR $=78-57=21$.
Team R has the smaller IQR, so its middle half is more consistent.

(a) Read the left whisker ends: Dataset E's minimum is $34$ and Dataset F's minimum is $51$. Dataset E has the lower minimum, $34$.
(b) Dataset E: range $=97-34=63$.
Dataset F: range $=97-51=46$.
Dataset E has the larger range.

examples.derivation: The plotted summaries are A=(13,29,46,63,88) and B=(19,38,52,59,81), with coordinates equal to 0.08 times each score. B has the higher median: 52>46. Ranges are 88−13=75 and 81−19=62; IQRs are 63−29=34 and 59−38=21. B has the more consistent middle half. A has the higher maximum: 88>81. Maximum and median describe different features. The supplied Guided Practice and question 1 support these methods.

The plotted summaries are C=(11,26,44,61,91) and D=(4,33,44,54,91), using the same 0.08 scale. Both medians are 44 and both maximums are 91. Ranges are 91−11=80 and 91−4=87. IQRs are 61−26=35 and 54−33=21. D therefore has the larger full range but the more consistent middle half. This follows the supplied comparison example.

The plotted summaries are Crew A=(16,23,31,42,54) and Crew B=(19,27,36,45,58), with coordinates equal to each time divided by 7.5. A has the lower median: 31<36 minutes. For B, 27<33<36 places 33 below the median, supporting the requested estimate of less than half below 33 minutes. At the median of 36 minutes, the conventional estimate is about 50% below. The repeated-value qualification appropriately limits exact-count claims. Source questions 2(e) and 3 support contextual median and threshold interpretation.

The plotted summaries are R=(7,18,26,35,43) and S=(43,57,69,78,94), using the common 0.08 scale. S has the higher median: 69>26. IQRs are 35−18=17 for R and 78−57=21 for S. R has the more consistent middle half despite its lower median. The supplied Guided Practice supports comparing typical values and consistency separately.

The plotted summaries are E=(34,45,65,80,97) and F=(51,60,70,85,97), using the common 0.08 scale. The left whisker endpoints give minima 34 and 51, so E has the lower minimum. Ranges are 97−34=63 and 97−51=46, so E has the larger range. Source question 1 supports endpoint reading and range comparison.
